case_title: Abdul Razak & Ors. v. State of Karnataka rep. by SHO, Hutti PS
accused_victim_relationship: Prior enmity/dispute: land and irrigation-water rivals of the victim's family (as alleged by the prosecution)
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.34 (charged); conviction under s.304 Part II r/w s.34 by High Court, not upheld by Supreme Court
weapon: Club of stones and stick (alleged); chilly powder thrown on face
evidence_type: Eyewitness (PW-1 and PW-4); documentary (fardbeyan Ex. P-1 and destroyed earlier report)
trial_court_outcome: Acquitted all appellants; prosecution failed to prove guilt
high_court_outcome: State appeal allowed; acquittal set aside; convicted under s.304 Part II r/w s.34 IPC; 7 years RI, fine Rs.5,000 each, default 1 year
neutral_facts: The prosecution alleged that the accused had a long-running dispute with the victim's family over the sale of a plot of land and the flow of irrigation water from a distributary, and that they demanded that the land be transferred to them and later demanded money for letting water flow. On the evening of the incident the victim was returning home when the accused allegedly caught hold of him, tied his hands behind his back, threw chilly powder on his face and assaulted him with a club of stones and a stick, causing injuries to the head and other parts of the body. The victim's brother and mother said they witnessed the assault from a nearby field. The brother said he moved to intervene but his mother dissuaded him. After the assailants left, the brother and mother went near the injured man but returned home. Later they went back to the field with the victim's father, who found the victim with his hands still tied, a leg injury and his eyes burning from chilly powder. The father went to lodge a report at a police post. A Sub-Inspector arrived at about 10.00 p.m. in a police jeep and recorded a written complaint from the brother as the first information, in which the victim was described as dead. The brother was then directed to untie the victim's hands, and the victim was taken to hospital, where he was found to have died on the way. The investigating officer later destroyed the report he had received about the incident after the brother's statement was recorded on the spot. A charge-sheet was filed against the accused.
physical_harm: Death of the victim from injuries to the head and other parts of the body; also a broken/fractured leg and eyes affected by chilly powder
number_of_offences: 1 charged (s.302 IPC r/w s.34); 0 finally upheld
motive: alleged: land-sale dispute and demands for money for irrigation water flow
key_evidence_accepted: Admission by the investigating officer (PW-19) that the original report was destroyed; the Court relied on this to reject the prosecution version. The eyewitness account was not accepted.
witness_credibility: Eyewitnesses PW-1 (brother) and PW-4 (mother) found unnatural and unreliable: they did not intervene, left the injured man tied, and waited for police. The Court agreed with the trial court's view.
post_offence_conduct: Accused left the spot after the assault; no other post-offence conduct of the accused is noted
trial_duration: offence: 19 September 2006; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 19 November 2012; Supreme Court: 15 May 2015
legal_representation: Accused (appellants): H. Chandra Sekhar, Anwesha Saha, Sharanagouda Patil, S-legal Associates; State (respondent): Anitha Shenoy, Ritwik Parekh
investigation_status: FIR registered (Crime No.168 of 2006); charge-sheet filed; trial completed
procedural_irregularity: Investigating officer destroyed the original report received about the incident after the fardbeyan was recorded on the spot
appeal_history: Trial court: acquitted. High Court: State appeal allowed; convicted under s.304 Part II r/w s.34 IPC, 7 years RI with fine. Supreme Court: appeals allowed; acquitted.
defence_argument: The accused alleged that the brother (PW-1), who had a money and land dispute with the deceased, was responsible for the injuries
legal_principle_applied: Prosecution must prove guilt beyond reasonable doubt; unnatural eyewitness conduct and the destruction of the original report render the prosecution version unacceptable
other_sentence_order: Appellants to be released from custody forthwith if not required in any other case
